newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST-St George half year net seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-St George half year net seen up.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd is expected to report a higher first half net profit next Tuesday, but the bottom line result is likely to be hit by a hefty restructuring charge following its merger with Advance Bank.

Analysts contacted by Reuters forecast St George to report a net profit after goodwill, preference dividends but before abnormals of between A$92.3 million and A$97 million for the six months ended March 31.
St George reported a pre-abnormal net profit of A$73.75 million in the 1995/96 first half and a A$148.3 million net profit for the 1995/96 year after preference dividends.

The first half results would include two months of earnings from its A$2.6 billion takeover of Advance Bank, completed earlier this year. Analysts said the net profit contribution from Advance is estimated to be around A$17 million.
They expected an abnormal loss of about A$75 million from restructuring charges following the Advance Bank takeover and subsequent closure of bank branches.

Michael Pulman, at brokerage firm ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, estimated net profit after goodwill and preference dividend at A$92.4 million for the first half, with preference dividend payments expected to total A$16 million.

One Sydney-based bank analyst forecast St George to report a first half net profit before abnormals of A$92.3 million, while a Melbourne-based brokerage forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$97 million for the half.
The analysts all agreed St George was likely to pay a 26 cents a share dividend payment for the half, unchanged from a year earlier.
The bank analysts said trading conditions for St George continue to be tight with intense competition in its traditional home loan market.
